comments.text: I was born and raised in São Miguel, Azores. No matter where I rest my head these days, that beautiful island will always be home.

replies.author: @melstiller8561
replies.text:
​@clauswilker4734--
How wonderful, Claus, that you have seriously considered buying property in São Miguel so you can settle there... 

And settle there you would. You would feel completely at home in no time at all. I still remember a German family owning property and living in Vila Franca do Campo -- São Miguel's original capital. Don't let my YouTube pseudonym fool you; I am Vilafranquense and 100% Portuguese. 

There is a very special rhythm to São Miguel, a pulse that is easily felt when you sit near the ocean and allow it to enter your soul. And the people -- oh the people! They're generous but strong, hardworking individuals who carry the indefatigable blood of mariners in their veins. 

São Miguel is also the birthplace of great writers and poets of yesteryear. Once upon a time, when I was a child, I was discovered as a poet -- a young Vilafranquense with a penchant for scribbling verses that my soul created and newspapers published. But this was all so very long ago...

Now that I am nearing the end of my journey (time forgets no one, Claus), I still write a lot of poetry (it's on YouTube) and carry the salt of the Atlantic Ocean in my veins. 

My love for my birthplace will never die.

replies.author: @clauswilker4734
replies.text: I was on Sao Miguel twice, and when my feet touched the tarmac at the airport the second time, I had such an overwhelming feeling of coming home my eyes got wet. Strange feeling for a tourist for sure, but then it was love at first sight. I still regularly check the available properties as I dream of opening the laptop in the morning breathing the freshest air I ever enjoyed.
